["Epidemiologi K3 (Occupational Health and Safety Epidemiology)", "The field of study that examines the frequency, distribution, and determinants of diseases is the most common definition used to describe the discipline of epidemiology. Epidemiologists systematically apply both deductive and inductive reasoning before drawing conclusions about events occurring within specific groups, particularly concerning diseases or health conditions affecting certain populations. This makes epidemiology an essential and indispensable field of study. Epidemiological studies aim to uncover cause-and-effect relationships between risk factors and specific diseases, thereby providing insights into the health status of populations. These findings are supported by analyzing field-based evidence and utilizing fundamental epidemiological measurements such as rates, ratios, and proportions. In terms of frequency measurement, this book discusses prevalence (point prevalence, period prevalence), incidence (incidence rate, incidence risk), and other key epidemiological assessments. This book is structured as a comprehensive synthesis of occupational health and safety epidemiology. Many critical aspects need to be considered when analyzing occupational health and safety (OHS) from an epidemiological perspective, ranging from the history of OHS epidemiology to the combination of risk prevention and control strategies through surveillance and risk assessment, among other topics.
